title: Triage models flag opioid misuse in an enriched retrospective emergency cohort
summary: First posted as a July 2025 preprint and journal-published in February 2026, this study reports machine-learning identification of opioid misuse from data available at emergency-department triage. Among 1,123 analyzed encounters, the latest 169 formed a temporal test set; gradient boosting reported AUROC 0.88, AUPRC 0.89 and F1 0.77 against expert chart-review labels. The single-center cohort was deliberately enriched for opioid misuse, and overlapping model confidence intervals and absent prospective or fairness validation limit claims about routine screening or patient benefit.
ai_technology: Random forest; gradient boosting; additional supervised classifiers on triage-time EHR features
organization: University of Illinois Chicago; University of Wisconsin Madison

evidence.tested: The retrospective cohort covered September 2020–March 2023 and was chronologically partitioned 70/15/15 for training, validation and testing. Models used structured triage/history data and expert-adjudicated labels. The latest 169 encounters were held out; gradient boosting achieved AUROC 0.88, AUPRC 0.89 and F1 0.77. Models performed comparably to opioid-related diagnosis codes entered by encounter end; these codes were not a triage-time comparator.
evidence.unknown: Enriched sampling does not estimate routine-population prevalence or predictive values. Most performance confidence intervals overlapped; model superiority was not established. The authors call for prospective multi-site calibration and bias/fairness checks before clinical trials. The demographic-table totals are inconsistent with the repeatedly stated 1,123 analyzed encounters; subgroup claims are not used.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised classifiers learn associations between information available at triage and manually assigned opioid-misuse labels, permitting temporal hold-out assessment of early identification without waiting for encounter-end diagnosis codes.

source_review.scope: Original journal full text: cohort selection, chronological partition, triage feature processing, model Methods, Results, limitations and date/preprint metadata; original medRxiv v1 metadata and abstract compared. Supplements not assessed.
